body:
This botanical comes from the Himalayan region where it lives on rocks like a lichen. It is similar in look to the edges of romaine lettuce. It doesn't have much of an aroma and just a slight rubbery feel.
I ripped the material it into small peices and made a cig using my manual cigarette machine. I filled one long cigarette tube.
I took two puffs and noticed giddiness. I felt happier, but by far the best part was that I couldn't think of the past or the future; I could only perceive what was going on in the present. This was remarkably strong for a few hours. I've tried the lesser entheogens to the point where I thought I'd seen it all, but Rock Blooms' insistance that I stay in the present moment was impressive.
I used to meditate for three hours a day in order to lift my mood and sink into the moment. Rock Bloom gets me there in a matter of five minutes. I'm sorry I didn't know about this when I worked in a highly stressful job. I think one of these cigs in the morning and one at noon would have reversed the chemistry of stress that made me sick and caused me to leave my profession.
Another result of the cig is that afterwards I am aroused and want to make love.
I've noticed, though, that the Blooms only work alone. When I tried to add other botanicals, it wasn't as good. She's not an ensemble player.
